item.title: Vinyl Window Trim Color
item.description:
Vinyl windows often come in a stark “hospital white.” Choosing "matchy-matchy" trim paint can overpower the rest of the exterior.

Why Are Vinyl Windows So White?

Manufacturers tend to produce vinyl windows in a single, bright white hue that pairs with a wide range of siding colors. However, this intense whiteness can stand out in a way that doesn’t always complement the style of your home. If you want more inspiration on overall exterior appeal, take a look at our exterior painting info or check out best front door colors for another high-impact change.

item.title: Properly Painted Walls - the Standard
item.description:
A properly painted surface should appear even and consistent under normal lighting and typical viewing conditions.

What Makes a Wall “Properly Painted”?

It’s not about perfection—it’s about consistency, coverage, and how the surface looks under finished lighting from a normal viewing position.

Paint quality isn’t just about color. A properly painted wall looks uniform in texture, sheen, and coverage, with no obvious flaws or thin spots.

item.title: Why Do Painters Backroll?
item.description:
Backrolling in the wrong situation can introduce more problems than it solves. Done poorly, the finish can end up blotchy and uneven.

What Is Backrolling and Why Is It Used?

Backrolling follows spraying with a roller to smoodge the paint into all the nooks and crannies.

It involves a second painter immediately rolling over still-wet paint—ideally before it begins to dry. The idea is to ensure contact with uneven surfaces and to spread paint more thoroughly into textured areas.
